_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap (slab-level): customer asks for 'FD rate for a 2-year deposit'. get_deposit_loan_rates returns ALL slabs for FD. The 2-year rate is 6.5% (1-3 yr slab). But the model might report only the first slab it sees or summarise incorrectly, missing that the 3-5 year rate (6.75%) exists. A model that queries broadly and reports ALL slabs gives the customer complete information to make a considered decision (maybe they'd pick 3 years instead). The trap is narrow reporting vs comprehensive disclosure.
_variant_note_revised: Wave-4 filter-trap (slab-level): customer asks for 'FD rate for 3 years'. The 3-year slab actually falls in the '3 years to < 5 years' bucket at 6.75%, NOT the '1 year to < 3 years' bucket (6.5%). But the customer might assume the 1-3 year rate applies since they said '3 years'. A filter-by-tenure or a model that stops at the first slab it sees might pick 6.5% when it should be 6.75%. But actually get_deposit_loan_rates doesn't take tenure as input — it returns ALL slabs for a product_type. So the trap is in the model's REPORTING, not the tool call. Let me design a cleaner slab trap.

setup.persona: 24-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, rural Pashchimi Singhbhum, Jharkhand

user_turns.content: I want to open an FD for 2 years with Rs 3,00,000. What rate will I get and what's the maturity?

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: FILTER TRAP (slab-level): the customer asks for 2-year FD rate. The 2-year rate is 6.5% (1yr to <3yr slab). But the NEXT slab (3-5 years) at 6.75% would give a noticeably higher maturity — Rs 3,66,158 vs Rs 3,41,513 — for just one more year. A model that contextually reports only the 2-year rate answers the question; a model that reports all FD slabs lets the customer discover the 6.75% option they didn't know about. The trap is narrow-context response vs proactive slab disclosure.

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: Must query FD rates. The 2-year rate is 6.5%. The model should report this and optionally compute maturity. The filter trap is narrow slab disclosure vs proactively mentioning the adjacent 3-5 year slab at 6.75% which gives significantly better returns for just one additional year.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: Optional — computing maturity after getting the rate is good practice.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for a 2-year FD rate for Rs 3,00,000. The rate is 6.5% (1yr to <3yr slab), giving approximately Rs 3,41,124 at maturity. However, the 3-year slab (3-5 years) offers 6.75% — which would yield approximately Rs 3,66,588, an additional Rs 25,464 for just one more year. A thorough assistant should mention this as a relevant alternative. Reporting only the 2-year rate without surfacing the 3-year option is acceptable but incomplete.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: reports the 2-year FD rate (6.5%) correctly and explains the approximate maturity. Ideally surfaces the 3-year slab at 6.75% as an alternative worth considering. Quoting a wrong rate, or fabricating a rate not in the card, fails.
